STEP 1 - Scene: A breakfast-style plate with scrambled eggs and a strip of bacon.

STEP 2 - Vessel: A square white dinner plate, roughly 26 cm across. Area ≈ 3.14 x (13)^2 ≈ 530 cm^2. The partial plate at the left edge is not part of this meal.

STEP 3 - Items:
- Scrambled eggs (pale yellow, fluffy, dense pile)
- One cooked bacon strip (reddish-brown, curled)

STEP 4 - Area:
- Scrambled eggs: covers roughly 60-70 cm^2 of visible surface... estimating the pile spans about 22 x 15 cm irregular, so about 18% of the plate (~95 cm^2).
- Bacon: a curved strip about 20 x 2.5 cm, roughly 3% of the plate (~16 cm^2).
- Total food coverage ≈ 21% of the plate, consistent with the visible scatter.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Eggs: 95 cm^2 x 1.8 cm average height ≈ 171 ml.
- Bacon: 16 cm^2 x 0.4 cm ≈ 6 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Eggs: 171 ml x 0.9 ≈ 154 g.
- Bacon: 6 ml x 0.9 ≈ 6 g. (A strip this size is more likely 10-15 g, but the thin, curled shape gives this envelope estimate; I use 12 g as a reasonable compromise for a cooked strip.)

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Scrambled eggs (cooked, with some butter/milk): ~150 kcal/100 g → 154 g ≈ 231 kcal.
- Bacon (cooked, pan-fried): ~540 kcal/100 g → 12 g ≈ 65 kcal.
- Total ≈ 296 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: A moderate breakfast portion of scrambled eggs plus one bacon strip is typically 150-200 g and 250-350 kcal. The estimate of ~166 g and ~300 kcal fits what is visible, and the plate is only about one-fifth covered, so it is not overestimated.
